title: Flow decline on dry days 8 to 13 rose after 1997 in 250 south-east Australian catchments
abstract: We test whether a known increase in dry-spell flow decline is limited to the first days after rain. We compare days 3-8 and 8-13 within the same events in CAMELS-AUS v2.03. In 250 south-east Australian catchments with positive endpoints, the late bounded decline index rose by 0.0195 between 1951-1996 and 1997-2021. Its joint 95% time and space interval was 0.0053 to 0.0356. The 2010-2021 rise was 0.0211 (0.0043 to 0.0393; 124 catchments). SILO rain, a stricter rain threshold and a zero-inclusive check also gave positive pooled late changes. The paired early-minus-late change was -0.0075 (-0.0176 to 0.0009), so the data do not clearly distinguish the two segment changes. An earlier placebo had an interval across zero. This shows a late within-event signature beyond constant flow scaling. It does not identify faster aquifer drainage or explain the annual water loss. Short dry spells, event selection, coarse matching, shared data and intervals with fixed support limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate results, joint draws, a figure and a numerical audit are supplied.

display.caption: Late flow decline increased in selected dry spells. The paired early-minus-late change is uncertain. Joint 95% time and space intervals hold matching support fixed.
